explanation: The highest-power term controls what a polynomial does at the far left and right. Even degree makes both ends go the same way (both up, or both down if a < 0); odd degree sends the ends in opposite directions. The sign of the leading coefficient a flips them. Step n through whole numbers to feel the even/odd pattern.
bullets: Even n: both ends point the same way; odd n: opposite ends.
a > 0 lifts the right end; a < 0 flips the whole picture.
Only the leading term matters for the far-left/far-right behavior.
